thread:
Sean Gallagher: kicking off the tiered SLOs + error budget work. couple quick logistics so we don’t churn:
1) owners for Hosted vs Dedicated SLO draft
2) where we’re putting SLI queries + validation notes
3) scheduling: 60m kickoff + weekly

I can host kickoff. Rafael/Aisha can you propose ownership split + where we want drafts to live? :slightly_smiling_face:

Rafael Mendes: yep. proposal:
- Hosted tier SLO draft: Aisha (primary), I’ll review + align w alerting/policy
- Dedicated tier SLO draft: I can take first pass w Lauren + platform folks (capacity/readiness bits)

for artifacts:
- canonical SLO definitions live in Confluence under eng-sre/slo-and-error-budgets (new section)
- queries + scratch = Drive doc (so we can iterate), then we promote “blessed” queries into slo-toolkit repo as examples

Aisha Bello: works for me. I’ll own Hosted SLIs + table (availability/success, 5xx, timeouts, streaming disconnect, latency p95/p99).

question: do we want to define streaming latency as TTFT vs end-to-end separately from day 1? I think yes, otherwise we’ll be fighting about “p99 latency” meaning.

Nikhil Sharma: +1 on TTFT vs total stream. from Hosted customer POV TTFT is the one they complain about first.

Lauren Bishop: for Dedicated, please make sure we include pool readiness/capacity signal as a separate SLI. customers don’t care if the API is “up” if their pool is stuck warming.

Priya Natarajan: re Dedicated: Mina/Ravi team can help define what “ready” means operationally (scheduler healthy + min free capacity + model loaded?). don’t let it turn into a bespoke thing per pool if we can help it.

Allison Grant: on queries + metrics: please don’t put the “final” definitions only in Drive. we need them in Confluence AND somewhere versioned.

suggestion:
- Drive = messy validation + screenshots
- Confluence = spec (definitions, exclusions, windows)
- GitHub (slo-toolkit) = reference implementation snippets + schema

Sergio Costa: +1. for dashboards I need stable metric names + label conventions asap.

also: where are we landing the initial PromQL / MQL? if we can standardize panels, it’s easier to templatize across regions.

Nadia Rahman: important: we need to decide up front what dimensions are “allowed” (tier/region/model/route) vs what gets aggregated to avoid cardinality blowups.

if we let everyone break down by request_id-ish labels, we’ll regret it.

Amara Diallo: on streaming disconnect: gateway logs today don’t differentiate client abort vs server-side disconnect cleanly. I can take an action item to propose classification + update metrics.

Aisha Bello: perfect. I’ll put in the Hosted doc that streaming disconnect SLI will depend on gateway classification and is “provisional” until instrumentation lands.

Talia Benson: scheduling: what time zones are we optimizing for? I can send a poll.

Sean Gallagher: let’s do PT/ET friendly, also keep a slot that works for Priya.

kickoff agenda:
- tier principles (Hosted vs Dedicated)
- SLI definitions + exclusions
- target-setting approach (backtest)
- enforcement phases (warn-only -> block)

Rafael Mendes: I’ll draft a Confluence skeleton today and share here.

for query location: I’ll create Drive folder:
Engineering > SRE > Tiered SLOs > “SLI validation scratchpad”

we can link it from Confluence so people don’t keep making new docs.

Allison Grant: please include a section in the spec for “measurement windows + rollups” (28d for budgets, plus 1h/6h burn windows for alerts). even if numbers TBD.

Sergio Costa: I can start dashboard folder structure in Grafana once we pick naming. eg:
SLOs / Hosted / <region>
SLOs / Dedicated / <region>

and top-level “Error Budget” summary dashboards.

Nikhil Sharma: can we keep “model catalog operations” in scope from the start? (model list, model version pinning) — those have been flaky and show up as onboarding failures.

Aisha Bello: yep, but might be separate SLO “journey” vs inference endpoints. I’ll add a section but targets may differ.

Lauren Bishop: for Dedicated, we should be careful on what’s excluded. eg customer-side timeouts shouldn’t count, but if the pool is saturated due to our autoscaler lag, that’s on us.

Priya Natarajan: agree. we’ll need a crisp definition for “capacity-related errors” vs customer misconfig. Ethan/Vanessa can help later but for now define the buckets.

Amara Diallo: I’ll post current gateway codes we see for disconnects in the scratchpad + proposal for mapping:
- client abort (499)
- upstream timeout
- upstream disconnect

Nadia Rahman: and please capture where timeouts are measured (gateway vs runtime). mismatch has bitten us.

Sean Gallagher: action items recap:
- Rafael: create Confluence skeleton + link Drive folder
- Aisha: Hosted SLO draft owner + include TTFT vs stream duration
- Rafael + Lauren: Dedicated SLO draft owner (include pool readiness)
- Amara: streaming disconnect classification proposal
- Sergio: draft dashboard structure + list required panels
- Talia: send kickoff + weekly poll

I’ll send a calendar hold for kickoff once Talia has a time.

Talia Benson: poll going out now (2 options). will include Zoom + doc links.

Rafael Mendes: Confluence stub created, dumping link here (WIP): https://confluence.redwoodinference.com/display/ENGSRE/Tiered+SLO+definitions+-+Hosted+vs+Dedicated

Drive folder: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1SLO-scratchpad-tiered

Aisha Bello: added initial Hosted outline + exclusions list. pls comment inline.

Sergio Costa: thanks. once metric names are confirmed I’ll start templating dashboards. if anyone’s changing label names (tier vs product_tier) pls flag early.

Sean Gallagher: awesome. keep thread updates here for now so kickoff isn’t a surprise. :thumbsup:
